knowledge_point.title: Solving a System of Equations Using Back Substitution

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=\frac{1}{2} \\ {x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=- \frac{3}{2} \\ {x}_{3} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=5.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-(5)=- \frac{3}{2}.
$$

$$
{x}_{2}=- \frac{3}{2}-(-5)=\frac{7}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=\frac{7}{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=5$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-2(\frac{7}{2})-(5)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}-(-7)-(-5)=\frac{25}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{25}{2}$, ${x}_{2}=\frac{7}{2}$, and ${x}_{3}=5.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}\frac{25}{2} \\ \frac{7}{2} \\ 5\end{bmatrix}.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=- \frac{27}{2} \\ {x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=\frac{9}{2} \\ {x}_{3} &=-3\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-3.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-(-3)=\frac{9}{2}.
$$

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{9}{2}-(3)=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=-3$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-2(\frac{3}{2})-(-3)=- \frac{27}{2}.
$$

$$
{x}_{1}=- \frac{27}{2}-(-3)-(3)=- \frac{27}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=- \frac{27}{2}$, ${x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}$, and ${x}_{3}=-3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}- \frac{27}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

$$

$$
{x}_{1}-2(- \frac{61}{2})-(-44)=\frac{439}{2}.

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{439}{2}-(61)-(44)=\frac{229}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{229}{2}$, ${x}_{2}=- \frac{61}{2}$, and ${x}_{3}=-44.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3} &=-4 \\ {x}_{2}-6{x}_{3} &=-32 \\ {x}_{3} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=4.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-6(4)=-32.
$$

$$
{x}_{2}=-32-(-24)=-8.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=-8$ and ${x}_{3}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+(-8)-(4)=-4.
$$

$$
{x}_{1}=-4-(-8)-(-4)=8.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=8$, ${x}_{2}=-8$, and ${x}_{3}=4.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{bmatrix}8 \\ -8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$
